content.glance: BNS s. 105 — Punishment for culpable homicide not amounting to murder.

sections.heading: The legal rule
sections.body: 105. Whoever commits culpable homicide not amounting to murder, shall be punished with imprisonment for life, or imprisonment of either description for a term which shall not be less than five years but which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine, if the act by which the death is caused is done with the intention of causing death, or of causing such bodily injury as is likely to cause death; or with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years and with fine, if the act is done with the knowledge that it is likely to cause death, but without any intention to cause death, or to cause such bodily injury as is likely to cause death

questionsAndAnswers.question: Legal Assessment & Statutory Note: BNS s. 105 (Punishment for culpable homicide not amounting to murder)
questionsAndAnswers.answer:
Introduction. BNS s. 105 deals with Punishment for culpable homicide not amounting to murder. It sits in Chapter VI — Of Offences Affecting the Human Body of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023. After 1 July 2024 this is the current-law citation for this offence / definition / punishment.

Meaning. Punishment for culpable homicide not amounting to murder (old 304). Part I — if the act is done with the intention of causing death or likely-to-cause-death injury: life, or up to 10 years, and fine. Part II — if only knowledge: up to 10 years and fine.

Legal rule. In student language: BNS s. 105 is the rule on “Punishment for culpable homicide not amounting to murder”. The section provides that whoever commits culpable homicide not amounting to murder, shall be punished with imprisonment for life, or imprisonment of either description for a term which shall not be less than five years but which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine, if the act by which the death is caused is done with the intention of causing death, or of causing such bodily injury as is likely to cause death; or with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years and with fine, if the act is done with the knowledge that it is likely to cause death, but without any intention to cause death, or to cause such bodily injury as is likely to cause death. Do not stop at the heading. An examiner awards marks for the ingredients, the explanations and the illustrations, not for writing the title alone.

Essential ingredients. An authoritative analysis must list them, not hide them in one paragraph:
1. Whoever commits culpable homicide not amounting to murder, shall be punished with imprisonment for life, or imprisonment of either description for a term which shall not be less than five years but which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine, if the act by which the death is caused is done with the intention of causing death, or of causing such bodily injury as is likely to cause death; or with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years and with fine, if the act is done with the knowledge that it is likely to cause death, but without any intention to cause death, or to cause such bodily injury as is likely to cause death

Illustration. Give one short original example (label it as an example) and apply the ingredients.

Limitations. Apply only the conditions written in s. 105. Do not import a defence from a different chapter unless the question requires it.

Consequence / punishment. Part I: life or 10 years + fine. Part II: up to 10 years + fine.

Connected sections. Read with BNS s. 100, BNS s. 101. A preliminary brief mentions the neighbour; comprehensive submissions explain the exact distinction.

Conclusion. BNS s. 105 is the complete current-law heading for Punishment for culpable homicide not amounting to murder. Define, list ingredients, use an illustration, note any explanation or exception, apply, cite. That is a complete statutory structure.

learningObjectives: Master the bifurcated sentencing scheme under BNS s. 105.

enhancement.definition: BNS s. 105 provides the punishment for culpable homicide not amounting to murder: if the act is done with the intention of causing death or causing bodily injury likely to cause death, the punishment is imprisonment for life, or imprisonment of either description up to ten years, and fine (Part I); and if the act is done with knowledge that it is likely to cause death, but without intention to cause death or likely fatal injury, the punishment is imprisonment of either description up to ten years, or fine, or both (Part II).
enhancement.legalPrinciple: Calibrates criminal punishment according to the hierarchy of mens rea, reserving life imprisonment for intentional homicides and capping non-intentional knowledge homicides at ten years.
statutoryFramework: Chapter VI — Of Offences Affecting the Human Body, BNS s. 105 (corresponding to IPC s. 304).
Part I (Intentional Limb): Act done with intention of causing death, or causing bodily injury likely to cause death — imprisonment for life, or imprisonment up to ten years, and fine.
Part II (Knowledge Limb): Act done with knowledge of likelihood of death, but without intention to cause death or likely fatal bodily injury — imprisonment up to ten years, or fine, or both.
Gateway: Encompasses culpable homicide under Section 100 that does not ascend to Section 101, or that falls within the five Exceptions to Section 101.
essentialIngredients: The accused caused the death of a human being.
The act amounts to culpable homicide not amounting to murder.
For Part I: The act was accompanied by intention to cause death, or intention to cause bodily injury likely to cause death.
For Part II: The act was accompanied only by knowledge that it was likely to cause death, without homicidal or fatal injury intention.
enhancement.detailedExplanation: Section 105 is the sentencing engine for culpable homicide not amounting to murder. A case reaches Section 105 through one of two legal routes: (1) the act satisfies Section 100 but does not meet the higher probability thresholds of Section 101; or (2) the act meets Section 101 but qualifies for one of the five statutory Exceptions (such as grave and sudden provocation or sudden fight). The section is split into two distinct tiers: Part I applies where there was intention (intention to kill or to cause bodily injury likely to cause death), exposing the offender to life imprisonment or up to ten years. Part II applies where there was no intention to cause death or fatal injury, but only subjective knowledge that the act was likely to cause death, capping the sentence at ten years imprisonment.
examples: Teaching example (Part I - Exception 1 Provocation): An accused, upon discovering his spouse in an adulterous act, is deprived of self-control by grave and sudden provocation and shoots the paramour with intent to kill. The case falls under Exception 1 to s. 101 and is sentenced under s. 105 Part I (up to life imprisonment).

Teaching example (Part II - Knowledge only): An accused strikes an elderly trespasser once on the head with a light stick during a boundary dispute, knowing that striking an elderly person on the head is likely to cause death, but without intending to kill or cause grievous injury. The skull fractures and death ensues. The accused is punished under s. 105 Part II (up to ten years).
distinctions: Section 105 Part I vs Section 105 Part II: Part I requires intention (carries up to life imprisonment); Part II requires only knowledge without intention (capped at 10 years).
Section 105 vs Section 106: Section 105 requires intention or knowledge; Section 106 applies where there was neither intention nor knowledge, only rashness or negligence.
problemApplication: Issue: Whether an accused who delivered a single fatal blow during a sudden mutual brawl without premeditation should be sentenced under s. 105 Part I or Part II.
Rule: If the blow was delivered with intention to cause bodily injury likely to cause death, it falls under s. 105 Part I; if delivered with knowledge only, under Part II.
Application: The medical evidence showed a deep aimed blow with a heavy cleaver, showing intention to cause likely fatal injury, but mitigating under Exception 4 (sudden fight).
Conclusion: The accused is sentenced under BNS s. 105 Part I.

Part I: Intentional homicides (imprisonment for life or up to 10 years, and fine).
Part II: Knowledge-only homicides (imprisonment up to 10 years, or fine, or both).
